shared_elements: apparent anthropomorphic/zoomorphic face or head in relief
justification: Both surfaces carry low-relief carving with curling volutes and what may be a stylised face or head, but A is a legible ordered composition — a standing elaborately costumed figure with headdress facing a smaller figure, framed by columns and blocks of square glyph signs — while B shows only an eroded, unframed cluster of curvilinear scrolls around a possible eye/muzzle with no discernible figure, no glyph grid and no baseline arrangement. The correspondence amounts to the generic fact of relief carving with curved motifs, which unrelated traditions could easily produce independently.
